svg.text: K3b DRUM AND BELT LINE (improved) — overview
A tilting, spinning drum and a washable belt cassette do the food work; one gantry hand moves vessels and passive tools.
est. cost: machine part ≈ €9.5–15 k + appliances ≈ €1.65 k
X box: hand rail, labyrinth slot (no seal)
TOP VIEW at deck and belt level
THE MEAL: Frikadellen with mash, 4 persons
mash: peeled, boiled, mashed in the drum
Frikadellen: mixed in drum, shaped on belt, fried
HOW THE FOOD FLOWS (active station highlighted)
colours: steel ware blue-grey · moving parts orange · water blue · heat red · raw mince red-brown · potato yellow

g.text: 1/8 The hand takes the mince box from the shelf under the ceiling port and tips it into the drum (mouth up, +60°)
2/8 The drum turns at +35° against the roller-scraper hung on its post: the Frikadellen mass binds (the hand stays free)
3/8 The drum tilts to −35° and pours the mass over its lip into the scoop; the hand tips it as a heap onto the red belt
4/8 The belt rolls the heap into a log under the curl hood; the comb divides it in 8 — meanwhile the drum washes itself (90 °C rinse)
5/8 Lay-down: the hand moves the pan under the belt nose at belt speed, the pieces drop in rows; the pan fries on the hob
6/8 Potatoes: box tipped into the clean drum; the drum spins them over its knurled disc (rumble-peel) and pours the slurry to the gully
7/8 The drum boils the potatoes (its coil heats the wall), drains to the gully at −10°, then mashes with the masher grid on its post
8/8 Plating: the hand holds a warm plate under the lip, the drum pours mash; Frikadellen added; the plate leaves through the side hatch
